scope: Standards-conformant NIP-59 transport for Bahia maintenance ContextVM requests and worker immediate responses.
intended_behavior: Bahia publishes every maintenance/* command as a standards-conformant stored NIP-59 gift wrap around a canonical ContextVM 25910 rumor.
The serialized relay event does not expose absolute host filesystem paths, the Bahia signer pubkey, or the inner JSON-RPC payload.
A high-entropy nonce remains inside each encrypted maintenance rumor so public event-id correlation cannot be used to confirm guessed path payloads.
The request receipt identifies the rumor id used by the worker response e-tag and advertises kind 1059 for request and immediate response.
The worker dual-reads legacy traffic during ordered rollout, mirrors the received wrapper format, and can explicitly reject non-NIP-59 traffic after cutover.
Maintenance ACL authorization and embedded Tier-2 approval verification continue to operate on the authenticated unwrapped requester and unchanged params.
out_of_scope: Implementing the downstream HygieneObservationSource tracked by fp-20aa.
Encrypting canonical 30315 status or 4903 audit events; those projections must instead omit path-bearing details.
